questions.stem: A subnet's route table has a default route pointing at a NAT gateway that sits in the same subnet. Instances in the subnet cannot reach the internet. What explains this?
questions.hint: Ask how the device doing the translation reaches the internet itself.

options.text: The NAT gateway must sit in a subnet that routes to an internet gateway
options.why: Correct — a NAT gateway needs its own path out, so it belongs in a public subnet.

options.text: NAT gateways only forward traffic once a secondary elastic IP is attached
options.why: Wrong — a NAT gateway takes exactly one elastic IP at creation.

options.text: The route table is missing an explicit rule for the VPC CIDR range
options.why: Wrong — the local route is created automatically and cannot be removed.

options.text: Security groups block outbound traffic until a rule is added
options.why: Wrong — security groups allow all outbound traffic by default.

questions.stem: A database needs sustained 40,000 IOPS on a single 400 GiB volume with consistent sub-millisecond latency. Which volume type fits?
questions.hint: Consider which family lets you provision IOPS well past the general purpose ceiling.

options.text: io2 Block Express SSD
options.why: Correct — it sustains this IOPS level at the required latency.

options.text: gp3 general purpose SSD
options.why: Wrong — gp3 tops out at 16,000 IOPS per volume.

options.text: st1 throughput-optimised HDD
options.why: Wrong — st1 is throughput-optimised HDD, unsuited to random IO.

options.text: sc1 cold HDD volumes
options.why: Wrong — sc1 is cold HDD, the lowest-performance option.

questions.stem: An application on EC2 must read from an S3 bucket in the same account. Which two steps grant access without long-lived credentials? (Select TWO.)
questions.hint: Two pieces are needed: one that permits the assumption, one that delivers the role.

options.text: Create a role with a trust policy allowing the EC2 service to assume it
options.why: Correct — the trust policy is what lets EC2 assume the role.

options.text: Attach the role to the instance through an instance profile
options.why: Correct — the instance profile is how a role reaches an instance.

options.text: Store an access key pair in the instance user data script
options.why: Wrong — this is a long-lived credential, which the question rules out.

options.text: Add the instance's private IP address to the bucket policy as a condition
options.why: Wrong — bucket policies match principals, not private addresses.

options.text: Enable an S3 gateway endpoint on the subnet's route table
options.why: Wrong — an endpoint changes the network path but grants no permission.

questions.stem: Which statement about network ACLs and security groups is accurate for a subnet hosting web servers?
questions.hint: Focus on which of the two controls keeps no memory of the connection that started a flow.

options.text: Network ACLs are stateless, so return traffic needs an outbound rule
options.why: Correct — statelessness is the defining difference from security groups.

options.text: Security groups evaluate rules in numbered order and stop at the first match
options.why: Wrong — that describes network ACLs; security groups evaluate all rules.

options.text: Network ACLs can reference a security group as a rule source
options.why: Wrong — only security groups can reference other security groups.

options.text: Security groups apply at the subnet boundary rather than the interface
options.why: Wrong — they attach to elastic network interfaces.

questions.stem: An archive volume is read once a quarter and holds 12 TiB. Throughput matters more than latency and cost must be lowest. Which volume type?
questions.hint: Weigh price against access frequency when the read is rare, large and sequential.

options.text: sc1 cold HDD volumes
options.why: Correct — cold HDD is the cheapest option for infrequent large scans.

options.text: st1 throughput-optimised HDD
options.why: Wrong — st1 costs more and targets frequently accessed throughput workloads.

options.text: gp3 general purpose SSD
options.why: Wrong — SSD pricing is unjustified for quarterly access.

options.text: io1 provisioned IOPS SSD
options.why: Wrong — provisioned IOPS is the most expensive choice available.
